mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) reduces the discount rate applied to equity cash flows, increasing present value of future earnings and generating positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns across all economic regimes.
failure_condition: Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a predictor of 20-day SPX returns remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window or average 20-day returns during low FEDFUNDS periods are not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 4.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending power and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 forward 5-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 4.5% (t-test p>0.05) or Rank IC for UNRATE as a 5-day predictor falls below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates severe economic contraction, triggering risk-off sentiment and negative S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: The INDPRO-UNRATE interaction term does not significantly predict negative 60-day SPX returns (t-test p>0.05) or Rank IC for the interaction signal remains below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and rising for 3 months), a decline in retail sales (RSAFS) signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: In monetary tightening cycles, RSAFS declines do not produce negative 20-day SPX returns (t-test p>0.05) or Rank IC for RSAFS in this regime falls below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A lower unemployment rate (UNRATE) reflects tight labor market conditions that support corporate profit growth and consumer spending, generating positive S&P 500 forward 5-day returns.
failure_condition: Rank IC for UNRATE as a 5-day SPX return predictor remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window or average 5-day returns during low UNRATE periods are not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1700.0 thousand units signals weakening housing market conditions, reducing consumer confidence and economic activity, causing negative S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not significantly negative when HOUST falls below 1700.0 (t-test p>0.05) or Rank IC for HOUST as a 60-day predictor remains below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in inflation (CPIAUCSL) and federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates aggressive monetary policy response to inflation, increasing real interest rates and compressing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: The CPIAUCSL-FEDFUNDS interaction term does not significantly predict negative 20-day SPX returns (t-test p>0.05) or Rank IC for the interaction signal remains below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions (GDP growth rate < 1.0% annualized), a decline in GDP (GDPC1) signals the end of the expansion phase, triggering recession fears and negative S&P 500 forward 5-day returns.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansions, GDPC1 declines do not produce negative 5-day SPX returns (t-test p>0.05) or Rank IC for GDPC1 in this regime falls below 0.03.
